Subject: Order form redlines — IP ownership and training carveouts

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement is reviewing the draft order form and legal had a few redlines around IP and training: principally, they want explicit assignment of "output" (customer-generated content) to Nova Product Labs and an opt-out for any model training or use of customer prompts. They also asked for an evidence checklist we can share with our InfoSec team (SOC 2, audit logs, data retention policy).

Two specific asks up-front:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the Order Form can state Nova retains title to generated output (text, code, assets)?
- We need a short evidence packet — SOC 2 report and a statement about whether Redwood would use customer prompts or outputs to improve models (and under what opt-in).

Attached: Nova_PO-Redlines_v1.pdf with inline annotations from our counsel.

Happy to hop on a brief call if easier. We aim to get a PO signed by next week.

Thanks,
Maria Torres
Procurement Manager | Nova Product Labs

Hi Maria — thanks for the notes and the redlines. Looping in Laura (Legal ops) and Ben (Contracts) to confirm contraints. Quick answers while they review:

- Output ownership: We can accept language that customers retain title to output they supply and the generated outputs from their prompts, subject to a limited license to Redwood to operate the service (below).
- Training: Redwood’s default position is no training on customer data without an explicit opt-in. We can add a clear opt-out checkbox in Exhibit A.

Ben/Laura — attaching our proposed Exhibit A template (OrderForm_ExhibitA.xlsx). Two items we need legal sign-off on and a short evidence bundle to send back to Nova’s InfoSec: SOC 2 scope statement, data retention window, and a short paragraph on telemetry/feedback handling (what we keep, for how long, and whether it’s used for model improvements).

I can be on a call tomorrow afternoon if helpful.

Best,

Subject: Fwd: Order form redlines — IP ownership and training carveouts 

Ben/Jordan — forwarding Nova’s redlines. High-level negotiating asks from the customer:

1) Customer wants title to output (generated artifacts) assigned to them.
2) Customer wants a firm commitment that Redwood will not use their prompts/outputs to train models (unless they opt-in).
3) They also want a compact evidence packet for InfoSec (SOC 2, data retention statement, logs/auditability).

My suggested positions to propose back:
- Output title: accept customer assignment of output, but include a narrow operational license to Redwood to store/serve content, run inference, and retain anonymized telemetry for SLOs and debugging.
- Training & feedback: accept explicit no-training-by-default; include an optional checkbox on Exhibit A for a training opt-in. For feedback (telemetry/error reports), propose a limited feedback license: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, revocable, royalty-free right to use de-identified telemetry and aggregated feedback for the purpose of improving Redwood’s service and model quality; Redwood will not use Customer prompts or outputs to train foundation models unless Customer opts in in writing."
- Evidence packet: we can provide SOC 2 type II summary, a short 1-page retention policy excerpt, and a redacted audit-log sample.

Action items:
- Ben: can Legal draft the exact order form language for Exhibit A around the feedback license + opt-in checkbox? Also confirm if the operational license wording above is sufficient for our support/hosting needs.
- Jordan: can you coordinate with Infra to prepare the SOC 2 summary and a redacted sample of request/response audit logs (no customer data) to send to Nova InfoSec?

Thanks — I want to keep the ask narrow so this doesn't blow up procurement lead times.

Rachel
Director, Legal Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Order form redlines — IP ownership and training carveouts

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear asks and the redlines. Rachel and I discussed and Legal can accept a customer-first outcome with the following compromise language. I put the redline into the attached PDF (Nova_PO-Redlines_v3.pdf) and updated Exhibit A. High-level points:

1) Output ownership: "Customer retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Content and Customer Outputs. Redwood is granted a limited, revocable license to store, transmit, cache and display Customer Outputs to provide the Service."

2) Training and feedback: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or improve foundation models, unless Customer provides an explicit opt-in in Exhibit A. For operational telemetry and error reports, Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use de-identified and aggregated telemetry solely to maintain and improve the Redwood service; such telemetry will not be used to train general-purpose foundation models."

3) Evidence packet: Attached is a SOC 2 Type II cover letter (summary), a one-page data retention excerpt, and a redacted sample audit-log template. We recommend sharing the SOC 2 summary and retention excerpt directly; the redacted log is available under NDA if needed.

If that wording looks good to Nova, we can incorporate the redline into the order form and send a DocuSign link for execution. If Nova needs training-restricted examples (e.g., field-level opt-outs), we can add checkboxes in Exhibit A per environment.

Attached: Nova_PO-Redlines_v3.pdf (pdf, 158 KB).

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Nova_PO-Redlines_v3.pdf (pdf, 158 KB)
